summary: This thesis investigates the application of guidance from external scoring functions to improve sampling in target-aware molecular diffusion models. Using TargetDiff on mutant p53Y220C, a surrogate affinity model is trained from docked generated molecules and tested for guiding reverse diffusion towards higher binding affinity. While the surrogate predicts affinity well on clean molecules, improvements in generation are limited. To understand this, PolyGen2D, a controlled synthetic testbed, is introduced to study guidance in simpler coordinate-based diffusion. Results suggest guidance is effective when the guidance model matches noisy intermediate states during reverse diffusion.
